text:
olivia: Brainstorm: instead of holding a reserved "slot" per request, what if we emit a short-lived admission token when the gateway accepts traffic. token can be redeemed by a retry within a tight window (50-200ms).
noah: token model sounds lighter-weight. how do we prevent churn when upstream stalls for seconds? token TTL would expire quickly, right?
olivia: yes TTL short. the idea is to reduce head-of-line blocking for new requests but give retries a tiny fast-path to re-enter the queue before contending normally.
kevin: different from reservation slots in that tokens are transferable? e.g., if a slow request finishes it could hand token to another of same tenant?
li: i'd avoid transferability. tokens should be per-request lease only. transfer creates weird accounting and attack vectors.
dana: streaming corner: token redeem semantics need to account for partial frames. we shouldn't permit replay; token redeem could instead try a cheaper replica or a fast-fallback model variant.
olivia: agree. token used => annotate request with X-Admit-Token and route-level hints. fallback decisions are local to gateway.
noah: metrics/billing: how to expose? do we charge for admitted-but-unused tokens?
kevin: proposal: don't bill for token issuance. bill only if token redemption results in additional backend capacity being consumed (i.e., a retry actually runs). emit metric token_issued, token_redeemed, token_expired.
li: safety: cluster-level token budget. if many nodes issue tokens during an outage, token storm can still overload backends on redemption. add global circuit that stops issuing tokens when cluster retry-success-rate dips.
dana: preemption: if token holder is idle and starts exceeding request progress threshold, gateway should auto-expire token. also emit trace events: admit:issued, admit:revoked, admit:redeemed.
olivia: config snippet idea:
```yaml
routes:
  - name: completion
    admit_token:
      enabled: true
      ttl_ms: 150
      max_per_100ms: 100
      redeem_policy: replica-first
```
noah: integration with hedging: hedging sends a speculative second request after X ms. tokens could be used to avoid hedging doubling requests by giving a retry fast requeue. we need to document when to prefer hedging vs token redemption.
kevin: I worry about pathological clients gaming token lifecycle by opening connections and waiting < ttl to cause constant token churn. need rate limit on token per origin/tenant.
li: security: internal-only header e.g., X-Internal-Admit: true and strip at egress. require mTLS on downstreams to accept token headers.
dana: testing: perf plan - run a chaos scenario where 30% of upstream replicas fail with 100-500ms outages. measure p50/p95/p99 for new requests and retries with tokens vs baseline. also test streaming where partial frames are sent then upstream flips.
deploy-bot: feature-flag rollout started: admit-token experimental = true on canary cluster at 1745570025 :gear:
olivia: next steps: write short RFC comparing tokens vs reservation-slots vs immediate hedging. include simulation graphs for high variance latencies and a table of failure modes.
noah: i'll take hedging comparison section. kevin and li can cover security and global budget algorithms.
olivia: thanks — i'll collect and post a follow-up RFC draft here in the next 24h.
